title: Quality-gate failure record (build-failure)
description: Appended by feature-implementer when the quality gate (./gradlew build && ./gradlew test && ./gradlew checkJavaFormat) fails. The coordinator reads the latest build-failure record per req_id to decide between retry (retry < 3) and system-design-expert escalation (retry == 3). Append-only; failures are not deleted on success — instead, a build-pass record is appended so the retry trail survives in the file.

retry.description: Retry counter for this design cycle: the number of build-failure records since the latest design-block, plus one. 1 on the first failure, increments on each subsequent gate failure. Counts build-failure records, not dispatch-starts (which are also written for review-processing and consultation resumes). Resets to 1 after a fresh design-block record (whether the original or a re-triage record with supersedes_record_at set).

failed_check.description: Which step of the quality gate failed. autofix-audit is the gate's design-doc audit (code-quality-gate § Autofix Audit Procedure); a record failing it carries abort_reason: "design-mismatch" so recovery routes to system-design-expert instead of an implementer retry.

error_output.description: Full error output from the failing command. Multi-line strings are fine; JSONL preserves newlines as \n.

attempted.description: Brief description of the change the implementer made before the failure surfaced.

partial.description: Optional flag set by the implementer when this record is a partial-artifact handoff (the dispatch reached its toolCallBudget before the quality gate ran). When true, the error_output field carries a progress description (which tests pass, which files have been edited, which acceptance criteria remain) rather than a failure description. The retry counter still ticks; the existing build-failure recovery path routes the next dispatch with the partial-artifact context. Absent or false records carry the default meaning (quality-gate failure).

abort_reason.description: Optional. When set, this record is an abort rather than a retryable failure or a partial-artifact handoff. The implementer declares early (instead of burning the 3-retry cycle) that retrying cannot help: the slice cannot be implemented as triaged, or the gate's autofix audit failed. The handoff-routing skill's Build-Failure Recovery short-circuits past the retry counter when abort_reason is set: wrong-shape-slice → route to product-requirements-expert for re-split; design-mismatch → route to system-design-expert for re-triage; prerequisite-missing → escalate to human. The implementer SHOULD also set retry to the value it would have set on a normal failure so the retry trail remains coherent. design-mismatch also covers an autofix-audit failure (failed_check: "autofix-audit") — an out-of-bounds or uncovered design-doc change that only system-design-expert may reconcile, since the implementer never modifies docs/. Absent means the record is a normal quality-gate failure (or partial-artifact handoff when partial: true).
